additional_requirements: depressive_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness (Criterion C)
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode (Criterion B)

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.

subtypes.Derailment or Loose Associations: A speech pattern of switching rapidly from one topic to another with no logical connection between thoughts.
subtypes.Tangentiality: Speech that deviates entirely from the question and fails to answer directly.
subtypes.Incoherence or Word Salad: Severe fragmentation of speech and sentence structure, making it nearly impossible to understand.
subtypes.Neologisms: Using made-up words that have meaning only to the individual.
subtypes.Clang Associations: Speech governed by sounds, such as rhyming, rather than the meaning of words.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) is characterized by a persistent combination of mood episodes meeting criteria for major depression along with psychotic symptoms such as delusions or hallucinations, with psychotic features present for a substantial portion of the illness and for at least two weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms. The depressive component typically involves sustained low mood, loss of interest, and other neurovegetative and cognitive changes, while the psychotic features may be mood-congruent or incongruent. Over time, the course can be episodic or chronic, often leading to functional impairment in work, relationships, and self‑care. It is distinguished from major depressive disorder with psychotic features by the persistence of psychosis outside mood episodes, and from schizophrenia by the prominence and duration of mood symptoms across the illness.

patient.stressor: About a year and a half ago, Christina took on a series of high‑end residential contracts while preparing for her contractor licensing exams, working late nights on job sites and then going straight to community theater rehearsals or painting in her home studio. The sustained pressure to grow her business, maintain her reputation for meticulous design work, and stay visible in the local arts scene gradually eroded her sleep schedule and left little time for rest or family life. Over the following months, coworkers and her husband noticed she became increasingly withdrawn on job sites, missed design details she normally prized, and started canceling theater commitments, yet she pushed herself harder to keep contracts from slipping. The condition became clinically significant when she began losing clients due to repeated mistakes and no‑shows, and after a tense meeting where a long‑time builder questioned her reliability, she broke down in front of her pastor, who urged her to see a psychiatrist when she described her internal experiences and how she could no longer trust her own judgment at work.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like there’s something going on behind the scenes on my jobs, like people are plotting around my designs, and no one can convince me otherwise.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: On almost every job now I’m convinced the builders and even the homeowners are secretly emailing each other about how to sabotage my layouts or steal my design ideas, and even when my husband shows me normal messages or contracts I still feel like there’s a separate chain I’m not allowed to see where they’re laughing at me and planning to push me out of the business.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: When I’m alone in a house laying tile or trying to sketch a design, I hear this man’s voice right behind me saying things like, “You’re messing it up again,” or “They all know you’re a fraud,” even though there’s nobody there and the job site is completely empty.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.
S021.manifestation: My husband and clients tell me I jump all over the place when I’m talking now, like I’ll start explaining a flooring estimate, then suddenly go off about how the theater director stole my scene ideas, then something about my pastor’s sermon, and I can see from their faces they’re lost but I can’t seem to pull my thoughts back to the original point.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: There are days on site where I just freeze in the middle of a room, holding a tile or a trowel, staring at the floor for long stretches and not responding when people call my name, and other times I’ll pace back and forth in the hallway, muttering to myself and checking the windows over and over like someone’s watching us from outside.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: Most of the time now I feel like a shell going through the motions—my face feels stuck, I barely talk unless someone drags words out of me, and even simple things like showering, answering texts from friends, or hugging my kids feel like they take more effort than I have.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to lose hours happily painting or rehearsing lines at the community theater, but over the last year I’ve stopped showing up, my canvases are gathering dust in the studio, and even landing a big contract doesn’t excite me anymore—I just feel flat and detached, like none of it matters.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I mostly just pick at food now and have to force down a few bites at dinner because I have no appetite, and my clothes hang looser on me even though I’m not trying to lose weight.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: No matter how much I sleep or lie on the couch, I wake up feeling like I ran a marathon the day before, and climbing a flight of stairs or unloading a few boxes of tile leaves me so drained I have to sit down and rest in the middle of the workday.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I walk into these expensive homes and feel like a total failure who has ruined every project I’ve touched, and I can’t shake this belief that I somehow caused all the problems in my family and even the financial stress at church, like my bad energy or decisions have poisoned everything around me and I deserve to be punished for it.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: Pretty much every day I catch myself thinking it would be better for everyone if I just didn’t wake up, and on my darkest days I’ve pictured driving my truck off the highway on the way to a job and felt almost relieved at the idea, even though actually doing it scares me enough that I end up calling my pastor or my husband instead.

add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_and_depressive_episod: When the voice is telling me I’m a fraud and I’m convinced the contractors are plotting against me, I’m also at my lowest—barely eating, dragging myself out of bed, and feeling completely hopeless about my work and my life at the same time.
add_requirements.depressive_episode_is_present_for_the_ma: Looking back over this whole stretch, the heavy depression—the emptiness, guilt, and not caring about painting or theater—has been there almost the entire time, even during the few short spells when the paranoia and voices quieted down a bit.
add_requirements.delusions_and_hallucinations_occur_for_2: There was a period late last summer when my energy and appetite had picked up a little and I felt less weighed down, but I was still absolutely convinced people were emailing behind my back about my designs and I kept hearing that man’s voice criticizing me on job sites.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: In the past year I’ve lost several big clients from missed appointments and half-finished jobs, pulled away from friends and theater completely, and my husband has had to take over a lot of the bills and household tasks because I can’t manage everything reliably anymore.
add_requirements.duration: This all really started to snowball not long after I took on those high-end contracts and began cramming for my licensing exam, so it’s been going on for a little over a year now.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: The paranoia about people plotting around my designs and the man’s voice criticizing me have been a regular part of my life for most of this past year, starting a few months after the work stress peaked.
add_requirements.depressive_episode_duration: My mood has been low, with that empty, guilty feeling and loss of interest in art and theater, for roughly the past year or so, ever since the long stretch of overworking and late nights began catching up with me.
